lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary for a typical U.S. finance application.

items.says: Use a tense consistent with a current role.
Give the caddying bullet less space than the finance experience.
Specify your responsibility or the tournament’s scale.
items.because: “Helped” does not show what you contributed.

items.says: Define what the 40% improvement measures.
items.because: It is unclear whether close time, hours spent, or another measure improved.

items.says: Check that the 40% figure is supportable.
Clarify your contribution to the investment decisions.
Check whether one discount rate was appropriate for every project.
items.because: The projects may have differed in risk.

items.says: Say whether the analysis identified causes or prompted decisions.
items.because: The bullet says only which variances met the 5% threshold.

items.says: Discounting free cash flow to equity at weighted average cost of capital mixes valuation approaches.
items.because: The cash flow and discount rate belong to equity and enterprise valuation approaches, respectively.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins cannot produce a group margin.
items.because: A group margin requires consolidated EBITDA and revenue, accounting for eliminations.

items.says: Define how the under-4% forecast error was measured.
Make the link between the forecast and the USD 40M early repayment defensible.
Check the two-year default claim against each loan’s seasoning.
items.because: The claim is supportable only for loans that have completed two years.

items.says: Distinguish your underwriting work from final approval authority.
Substantiate the approval-rate comparison.
Substantiate the period used to assess early defaults.
“Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in 2022.
Clarify whether you created, maintained, or introduced the checklist.
Specify how the 6-to-3-hour reduction was measured, if known.
Do not present proximity to market price as proof the valuation was accurate.
State which direction the discount-rate change went.
Explain what the USD 52 and USD 44 figures represent.
Check that the spring pitch date fits the project timeline.
items.because: The project is listed as ongoing.

items.says: Remove the FP&A bullet unless it was genuinely an FP&A assignment.
items.because: It does not fit the stated fund role.

items.says: The FP&A bullet is generic.
The cash-forecast achievement repeats the Stonebridge bullet despite being dated years earlier.
items.because: Both cite a USD 600M business, roughly 4% error, and USD 40M debt repayment.

items.says: Listing only Excel may undersell your capabilities.
items.because: You may have used other relevant systems.
